payload.purpose_context: This mission advances charter write roundtrip latency on main so stakeholders can track the work from mission creation onward.

payload.wp_title: Cheap, exact document equality and a single-pass section writer
Repository-scale regression tests: round-trip count and runner-relative timing
One write cycle per compiled-charter refresh
Record the justified budget and tell users what improved

Tests: tests/charter/ full tree 4867 passed / 21 skipped; mypy clean; ruff clean. KNOWN CROSS-WP RED, closed by WP02: tests/architectural/test_no_dead_symbols.py::test_no_public_symbol_in_all_is_unimported and tests/architectural/test_dead_symbol_allowlist_contract.py both flag the new public prepare_charter_yaml_sections because it has no src/ caller until write_compiled_charter adopts it in WP02. Also found a pre-existing defect the corpus exposed: the old serialise-and-reparse rule RAISED (ScannerError) instead of answering on documents with a comment before a block sequence; the new rule answers. Covered by test_the_new_rule_answers_where_the_old_one_raised.

- 2026-10-31T15:30:23Z – claude – shell_pid=1655914 – Implemented. write_compiled_charter prepares catalog+metadata in ONE cycle via prepare_charter_yaml_sections(sections_from_document=...); _preserved_generated_at became _preserved_generated_at_in(document, catalog) and is decided from the document the write replaces (the path-taking wrapper was deleted: nothing else called it, and keeping it would have been dead surface). New test test_compiled_charter_single_cycle.py proves byte parity with a reconstructed two-cycle path, no-op idempotence (bytes and mtime unchanged, generated_at not restamped), and counts 1 prepared write / 1 render per refresh against a same-fixture two-cycle control (2 and 2). Tests: tests/specify_cli/cli/commands/charter/ + tests/specify_cli/charter_runtime/ + tests/charter/test_compiler_charter_yaml.py + the WP01 sections test = 738 passed, 2 skipped; the new file 5 passed. mypy and ruff clean. MEASURED (interleaved, same launcher, --repo-root, 5 rounds, project seeded from this repo's own .kittify, XDG cache isolated): charter list floor base 2.62s / head 2.77s (unchanged, as expected -- it does not touch the write path); charter deactivate base median 16.65s / head median 10.39s = ratio 0.624. Instrumented attribution of the same command: write_compiled_charter 9.14s -> 2.79s (3.3x), prepare_charter_yaml_section 2 calls -> 1, yaml_documents_equal 19 calls in 3 ms (was ~3.4 s), compile_charter unchanged at 2.4-2.5 s. NFR-001's 0.6x target is NARROWLY MISSED at 0.62; the remainder is the ~2.7 s read floor (already above the charter's 2 s budget on its own) plus the 2.5 s compiler pass that C-004 puts out of scope. Recorded honestly for the ADR in WP04 and flagged for the operator.

reason: Reviewed as reviewer-renata: approved. Diff is 24/16 lines in one function plus the preserved-timestamp helper; the Landmine-3 contract is intact (only the DERIVED catalog/metadata sections are written, charter.md untouched), the bootstrap branch is untouched, and the post-write tail (provision_mission_types then restamp_bundle_hash, #6366) keeps its order. - 2026-10-31T16:03:46Z – claude – shell_pid=1941545 – Implemented, with one recorded deviation from the WP's owned_files. T008's count test lives at tests/charter/activation/test_charter_write_roundtrips.py, not under tests/performance/, because .github/ci-module-registry.yml shows no per-PR lane selects tests/performance (only the nightly -m performance job does), and a structural gate that never runs on a PR is not a gate. Measured with the committed probe on a project seeded from this repo's own .kittify: 6 whole-document round trips for one merged write, 18 for the two-cycle shape it replaced -- the same-fixture control proves the probe can see the regression. That 6 replaces the plan's estimated 'at most 2 (from 10)' (which was a profile estimate, not a count); spec NFR-002/SC-002 corrected to the measured values and the analysis report re-recorded. T009: tests/performance/test_charter_write_repo_scale_timing.py, timing+performance marked, ratio over a read floor sampled interleaved in the same run, limit CHARTER_WRITE_RATIO_LIMIT in tests/_perf_helpers.py. Observed ratios: activate 3.71, deactivate 3.4-4.6 across series. The limit is 8.0 and is documented as a RUNAWAY guard, not the regression gate: at 4-6x the floor the command's own variance dominates, so no limit separates the pre-fix 16.7 s from the post-fix 10.4 s reliably on a shared runner (measured pre-fix series ranged 3.5-6.8). tests/architectural/test_perf_limit_authority.py and test_performance_marker_guard.py both pass with no allowlist entry. Run: tests/charter/activation/test_charter_write_roundtrips.py 2 passed; tests/performance/test_charter_write_repo_scale_timing.py 1 passed in 189s; ruff clean.

reason: Reviewed as reviewer-renata: approved. The count test measures the right thing at the right boundary (load/compose/scan of a document-shaped payload, recognised by the document's own header rather than by length, which a write changes) and drives the production function the activate command invokes rather than a helper. Non-vacuity is proven by a same-fixture two-cycle control measuring 18 against the budget of 6, so the assertion cannot pass with a blind probe. The 6 replaces the plan's estimated 2, and the spec was corrected and the analysis report re-recorded rather than leaving a falsified NFR. The timing test obeys ADR 2026-10-05-2 (interleaved ratio, limit in the one authority, no seconds) and says plainly that it is a runaway guard, not the regression gate -- which is the honest reading of the measured data (pre-fix series ranged 3.5-6.8, post-fix 3.4-4.6, so no limit discriminates them). The one deviation, the count test's home under tests/charter/activation, is justified in the commit and the WP history: ci-module-registry.yml shows tests/performance is selected only by the nightly job.

- 2026-10-31T16:18:14Z – claude – shell_pid=2119532 – Implemented. ADR docs/adr/4.x/2026-10-31-1-charter-write-budget-for-repository-scale-projects.md records the read floor (2.62-2.77 s, already above the 2 s charter budget on its own), the interleaved before/after medians (16.65 s -> 10.39 s, five rounds, ratio 0.624), the structural round-trip count (18 -> 6), the six considered options with the real reason each was rejected, and the two questions the operator owns (whether 8x is the right runaway bound; whether the incremental-catalog-update work should be chartered separately). Changelog entry under [Unreleased] / Fixed, 1,181 characters, impact-first with before/after and (#6506). Generated surfaces regenerated and verified: freshen_adr_inventory --all (row added to docs/adr/4.x/index.md), docs_index --write, check_docs_freshness --ci = errors=0 (the 5 remaining warnings are pre-existing: HELP-DRIFT for migrate ledger / service status / charter activate --only, all present on origin/main, plus external link-health probes). tests/docs/ + tests/architectural/test_no_legacy_terminology.py: 1900 passed after fixing three of my own docs-gate findings (ADR description 228 chars -> under the 180 band; 'serialised' -> 'serialized' in the changelog). No absolute seconds were added to any test.

reason: Reviewed as reviewer-renata: approved. The ADR answers the question the issue asks (why 9-15 s and not 2 s) in the Decision section rather than burying it, every figure is either traceable to a committed test (the round-trip count, the ratio limit) or explicitly labelled as a one-off interleaved measurement with its method and sample count, and the two rejected options that matter most (delete the equality checks; raise the 2 s budget) carry their real reasons rather than strawmen. It is consistent with ADR 2026-10-05-2 and cites it instead of restating it, and it does not touch the charter's own budget. It also states the uncomfortable finding plainly: the ratio measured 0.624 against a 0.6 target, and the remaining time is a read floor that already exceeds 2 s plus a compiler pass this mission put out of scope. The changelog entry is under 1,200 characters with an impact-first lead, before/after and (#6506), and the generated surfaces verify clean (check_docs_freshness --ci errors=0; the 5 warnings are pre-existing drift present on origin/main).
